text:
KINNAIRD COUNTY SCHOOLS
Office of Special Education and Preschool Services
412 Courthouse Hill, Ledford, KY 41766 | Phone (606) 555-0134 | Fax (606) 555-0135

ADMISSIONS AND RELEASE COMMITTEE (ARC) SUMMARY
Preschool Eligibility Determination - Developmental Delay
Confidential student record (707 KAR 1:350)

STUDENT INFORMATION
Student: Harlow Jean Halcomb          Goes by: Birdie
DOB: 04/11/2023   Age at evaluation: 3 yrs 4 mos   Sex: F
SSID: 2304417765   Local ID: KC-08812   Medicaid ID: 8820319044
Home address: 1186 Tinker Fork Road, Orrick, KY 41783
Parent/guardian: Shawna Halcomb (mother), cell (606) 555-0187
Parent email: shawnahalcomb93@gmail.com
Emergency contact: Loretta Jent (maternal grandmother), home (606) 555-0119
Current setting: Orrick Head Start, 3-year-old room (teacher Brittany Napier)
Proposed placement: Orrick Elementary School, Preschool Room 4
Notice of ARC sent: 09/03/2026   ARC meeting: 09/17/2026

1. REASON FOR REFERRAL
Harlow was referred through Child Find on 06/18/2026 by Ms. Napier after her spring DIAL-4 screening fell below cutoff in language and motor. Her mother reports Birdie says about 15 single words, mostly animal sounds and "Mamaw," and falls often on uneven ground. Consent for evaluation was signed 07/14/2026.

2. RELEVANT HISTORY
Harlow was born at 29 weeks gestation at Laurelwood Regional Medical Center and spent seven weeks in the NICU. Primary care is with Dr. Joanna Pelfrey at Tinker Valley Pediatrics. She received First Steps developmental intervention from 03/2024 to 11/2024; services stopped when the family lived in a camper on her grandmother's land for four months after the creek flooded the house. PE tubes were placed 01/22/2025 by Dr. Martin Oyler at Kinnaird ENT Associates. Harlow lives with her mother and her twin brother, Hayes, who is developing typically. Her father is not involved. Mom drives a concrete mixer truck for Orrick Ready Mix from 6:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., so Mrs. Jent keeps the twins on non-school days and takes them to the Wednesday night nursery at Lower Tinker Fork Freewill Baptist Church.

3. ASSESSMENT RESULTS
Battelle Developmental Inventory, Third Edition (BDI-3), 08/26/2026, Travis Begley, Ed.S., School Psychologist
Domain              DQ    SD from mean    Percentile
Adaptive            82    -1.20           12
Social-Emotional    80    -1.33            9
Communication       68    -2.13            2
Motor               74    -1.73            4
Cognitive           86    -0.93           18
BDI-3 Total         75    -1.67            5

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), 08/28/2026, Carla Spicer, M.S., CCC-SLP
Auditory Comprehension SS 72 | Expressive Communication SS 64 | Total Language SS 66 (1st percentile)
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3): SS 58; sound inventory limited to /m, b, p, d, n, w/
Vineland-3 parent interview, 09/02/2026: Adaptive Behavior Composite 77
Hearing: OAE pass both ears, Type A tympanograms (08/20/2026, Kinnaird ENT Associates)
Vision: SPOT vision screener pass (08/20/2026)

Classroom observation, 08/31/2026 (Misty Cornett, preschool teacher): Birdie played next to peers but did not join pretend play. She requested by pulling adults by the hand and pointing. She climbed the three-step slide with one hand held, walked with a wide base, and fell twice on the mulch. She held a fat crayon in a fisted grasp and did not imitate a vertical stroke. Work samples labeled H.J.H.

4. ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION (707 KAR 1:310)
Criteria per 707 KAR 1:002: at least 2 SD below the mean in one area, or at least 1.5 SD below the mean in two or more areas.
- Communication: -2.13 SD (meets the two standard deviation criterion)
- Motor: -1.73 SD (meets 1.5 SD in a second area)
- Adaptive, social-emotional: concerns, criterion not met
Exclusionary factors (hearing, lack of instruction, limited English proficiency) ruled out.
ARC DECISION: ELIGIBLE - DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY (communication, motor)

5. SERVICES, PLACEMENT AND LRE
Service                         Minutes        Location
Specially designed instruction  120 min/week   Early childhood classroom
Speech-language therapy         60 min/week    Classroom/therapy room
OT consultation                 30 min/month   Classroom
Transportation                  Daily          Special transportation with child safety seat
Birdie will attend the blended preschool/Head Start classroom 4 days per week with typically developing peers. ESY will be considered at the annual review.

6. ANNUAL GOALS
Communication: Given a choice of two pictured items, Harlow will request using a word, sign or picture in 8 of 10 opportunities across 3 consecutive data days.
Gross motor: Harlow will walk up and down 4 stairs with one hand on the rail, alternating feet on the way up, in 4 of 5 trials.
Fine motor: Harlow will imitate vertical and horizontal strokes with a crayon in 3 of 4 trials.

7. PARENT INPUT
Mrs. Halcomb said she "knew something was off at the one-year shots" and wants Birdie to be able to tell her when something hurts. She asked that the twins ride the same bus and prefers texts during work hours.

title: School-Based Occupational Therapy Evaluation Report, Grade 2 (fictional test record)
text:
PRUITT COUNTY SCHOOLS
Exceptional Children Services - Related Services Unit
1450 Depot Street, Canebrake, KY 41831 | (606) 555-0151

OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY EVALUATION REPORT
Initial School-Based Evaluation (707 KAR 1:300) - School Year 2026-2027

Student: Jaxon Tate Mullins          Preferred name: Jax
Student #: 300571     SSID: 1189034526     Medicaid ID: 7710458823
DOB: 11/03/2018       CA at testing: 7 years 10 months
Grade: 2              School: Quillen Elementary School
Classroom teacher: Amanda Sturgill    Case manager: Lacey Hensley
Parents: Corey Mullins and Ashley Mullins
Mailing: HC 64 Box 1127, Quillen, KY 41838
Physical: 4410 Big Mabry Fork Road
Home (606) 555-0162   Mother cell (606) 555-0148   Email: ashleymullins.jaxmom@yahoo.com
Referral: 08/24/2026   Consent: 09/01/2026   Testing: 09/10/2026, 09/14/2026   Report: 09/22/2026
Evaluator: Kendra Ritchie, MOT, OTR/L

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Jax was referred by Mrs. Sturgill through the school MTSS team for illegible handwriting, slow copying, frequent pencil breakage, and trouble managing lunch items and his coat. He is also being evaluated for a suspected learning disability in written expression.

BACKGROUND
Information is from parent interview (09/08/2026), school records, and teacher report. Jaxon was diagnosed with ADHD, combined type, in 03/2025 by Dr. Samuel Whitt at Pruitt Pediatric & Family Care and takes medication before school. He lost the tip of his left index finger in a log-splitter accident at age 4; the injury was treated at Pruitt County Medical Center. He writes with his left hand and holds the paper with his right. He repeated kindergarten. His first grade teacher, Renee Gilliam, noted reversals and avoidance of coloring. Vision and hearing screenings were passed 08/19/2026 (school nurse Teresa Collier, RN).
Jax lives with his parents and two older sisters on Big Mabry Fork. His father is a lineman for Mabry Valley Rural Electric and his mother works night shift as a CNA at Quillen Health & Rehab. Mrs. Mullins describes him as "busy from the minute his feet hit the floor." He helps his dad raise bluetick coonhounds and rides a four-wheeler to the bus stop. His children's church teacher at Big Mabry Fork Church of God told the family he will not color with the other kids.

ASSESSMENTS ADMINISTERED
- Bruininks-Oseretsky Test of Motor Proficiency, Second Edition (BOT-2), fine motor and upper-limb subtests
- Beery-Buktenica Developmental Test of Visual-Motor Integration, Sixth Edition (Beery VMI-6)
- Sensory Profile 2: Child Sensory Profile 2 (caregiver) and School Companion (teacher)
- Handwriting sample, near-point and far-point copying
- Clinical observation and classroom observation (09/11/2026, writing block)

BOT-2 RESULTS (subtest scale scores: mean 15, SD 5; composites: mean 50, SD 10)
Subtest / Composite            Score    Percentile   Category
Fine Motor Precision           6        --           --
Fine Motor Integration         7        --           --
Fine Manual Control composite  34       5            Below Average
Manual Dexterity               8        --           --
Upper-Limb Coordination        10       --           --
Manual Coordination composite  40       16           Below Average

BEERY VMI-6 (standard scores: mean 100, SD 15)
Visual-Motor Integration       76       5            Low
Visual Perception              91       27           Average
Motor Coordination             71       3            Low

SENSORY PROFILE 2
Caregiver: Seeking - Much More Than Others; Avoiding - Just Like the Majority; Sensitivity - More Than Others; Registration - Just Like the Majority.
School Companion: Attention - More Than Others; Behavior - Much More Than Others; Auditory - More Than Others; Visual - Just Like the Majority.

HANDWRITING AND FINE MOTOR
Jax uses a thumb-wrap grasp with heavy pressure and broke his pencil lead four times during testing. On near-point copying he copied a 12-word sentence in 3 minutes 50 seconds; 58% of letters were legible, with b/d reversals and no consistent spacing. Seven of 26 lowercase letters were formed from the bottom up. Far-point copying of the same sentence took 6 minutes 40 seconds. He cut a 6-inch circle within 1/4 inch of the line for about half its length. He could not tie his shoes or start his coat zipper, and needed help opening his milk carton and ketchup packet at lunch.

POSTURE, ATTENTION AND SENSORY
Jax W-sits on the carpet, slumps at his desk, and wraps his feet around the chair legs. He held prone extension for 8 seconds and supine flexion for 5 seconds. During the writing block he left his seat 9 times in 35 minutes, chewed his shirt collar, and settled after a 2-minute movement break.

SUMMARY
Jaxon shows below-average fine manual control, weak visual-motor integration with intact visual perception, low postural endurance, and sensory seeking that affects attention to written work and independent self-care at school.

RECOMMENDATIONS (for ARC consideration)
1. Occupational therapy as a related service: 30 minutes per week direct (push-in or pull-out) and 15 minutes per month consultation with the classroom teacher.
2. Proposed goal: copy a two-sentence near-point model with 80% legible letters and correct spacing in 4 of 5 samples.
3. Proposed goal: open lunch containers and start the coat zipper independently on 4 of 5 days.
4. Accommodations: pencil grip, slant board, raised-line paper, near-point copy, movement break every 20 minutes, wiggle cushion, and extended time (1.5x) on written assignments.

EYE CONDITION AND MEDICAL
Diagnosis: congenital aniridia, both eyes, with nystagmus; glaucoma in the left eye managed with drops after a trabeculectomy on 06/03/2025. Eye exam 07/21/2026 with Dr. Priya Raman, Lakemont Eye Institute: distance acuity 20/400 OD, 20/300 OS, 20/300 OU with correction. SECTION A. STUDENT AND FAMILY
Student: SPURLOCK, BRAYDEN COLE          Nickname: Spud
DOB: 07/19/2010    Grade: 11    SSID: 1076653490    IC#: 211408
Home school: Tolliver County High School
Address: 297 Upper Lick Branch Road, Dorcas, KY 41764

Email: mspurlock@tolliver.kyschools.us (mother is district staff; family prefers this address)

SECTION B. MEDICAL STATEMENT SUMMARY
Diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma of the left femur, diagnosed 05/28/2026. Treating physician: Dr. Elena Marchetti, Pediatric Hematology/Oncology, St. Brendan Children's Hospital, Halvorsen. MRN: SB-4471902.
Medical statement for home/hospital instruction signed 08/04/2026; received by the district 08/06/2026.
Reason student cannot attend: immunosuppression from chemotherapy given in alternating cycles every 2 weeks; planned limb-salvage surgery with an internal prosthesis on 10/20/2026; non-weight bearing for 6 to 8 weeks after surgery.
Anticipated duration: 08/10/2026 through 01/15/2027, with an updated medical statement every 60 days (next due 10/05/2026).
A central line port is in place; the teacher will not handle any medical equipment.

SECTION C. IEP AND STUDENT PROFILE
Brayden was found eligible under Other Health Impairment on 07/30/2026 after the ARC reviewed medical information and teacher reports of fatigue, low stamina, and attention problems related to treatment. Prior to diagnosis he had no IEP and was an A/B student. The ARC met 08/07/2026 to add home/hospital instruction as a change of placement.
Brayden is a junior who was the starting catcher on the varsity baseball team and serves as FFA chapter vice president. After his diagnosis the whole team shaved their heads, and the community held a benefit bean supper and gospel singing at Lick Branch Old Regular Baptist Church, where his father is the pastor. His mother teaches fourth grade at Lick Branch Elementary. His younger sister is a freshman cheerleader. The family drives about three hours each way for chemotherapy and stays at the hospital family house during inpatient cycles.

SECTION D. INSTRUCTION SCHEDULE
Homebound teacher: Rodney Gayheart (certified, social studies)
In-person visits: Tuesday and Thursday, 3:30-5:30 p.m., at home = 4 hours/week
Live virtual sessions: Monday and Wednesday, 4:00-5:00 p.m. = 2 hours/week
Special education teacher consultation with the homebound teacher: 30 minutes/week (Jared Pigman, ARC chair)
Total instruction: 6 hours per week, adjusted around the chemotherapy calendar; no instruction on days 1-3 of each cycle unless the family requests it.
During inpatient stays the hospital school teacher at St. Brendan, Paula Varney, provides instruction and emails a weekly log to the homebound teacher.

SECTION E. COURSE PLAN (fall semester)
Course                    Teacher            Delivery / modifications
English III               Shannon Brewer     Essential standards; audiobook texts; essays shortened to 2 pages
Algebra II                Phillip Coots      Guided notes; video lessons; homebound teacher proctors unit tests
U.S. History              Dana Holbrook      Taught by homebound teacher; document-based questions replace projects
Chemistry                 Megan Kilgore      Virtual labs replace wet labs; lab reports reduced
Ag Power and Technology   Wesley Cundiff     Shop hours waived; safety unit and small-engine diagram project
All 5 courses are on track for credit if 80% of essential assignments are completed by 01/15/2027.

SECTION F. ACCOMMODATIONS
Extended time (2x) on assignments and tests; tests broken into segments; rest breaks as needed; flexible due dates tied to the treatment calendar; copies of class notes and recorded lessons; reduced written output with oral responses accepted; school-issued hotspot (home internet is unreliable up the hollow).

SECTION G. HEALTH AND SAFETY PROTOCOL
- Family texts the homebound teacher by noon on visit days if counts are low or there is a fever; the visit moves to virtual.
- Teacher does not visit if ill or recently exposed; wears a mask during visits; washes hands on arrival.
- Fever of 100.4 F or higher: family follows the oncology team plan and the session ends.
- Emergency: call 911, then the parent cell numbers above.

SECTION H. ATTENDANCE AND RETURN TO SCHOOL
Coded home/hospital and counted present for each day instruction is delivered. Re-entry planning begins when Dr. Marchetti releases him, expected 02/2027. Return supports: half days for 2 weeks, elevator key, second set of textbooks, leave class 5 minutes early, rest area in the nurse's office. Accommodations for the state ACT in 03/2027 will be requested by the school test coordinator.

BACKGROUND FOR THIS REPORT
Gunner was placed at Ridgeview Academy after he struck an assistant principal during a hallway altercation on 02/26/2026. He is on juvenile probation following that incident. He has lived with his grandparents since 06/2023, when custody was granted; his mother is in a residential recovery program and his father was killed in a mine roof fall when he was 8. He works Saturdays at his uncle's sawmill, Bowman Brothers Sawmill, and builds and races go-karts. Staff use these interests in his reinforcement menu.

GOAL 1 - Coping / replacement behavior
When given corrective feedback or a non-preferred task, Gunner will use a replacement strategy (break card, request to walk, calm corner) instead of verbal aggression in 80% of opportunities for 4 consecutive weeks.
Baseline (02/2026): 25% of opportunities
Week of      Opportunities   Strategy used   Percent
08/17/2026   14              4               29%
08/24/2026   12              5               42%

09/07/2026   11              6               55%
09/14/2026   12              6               50%
09/21/2026   13              8               62%
09/28/2026   11              7               64%
Progress: Adequate progress. Upward trend; goal not yet met.

GOAL 2 - On-task behavior
During core academic blocks, Gunner will be on task in 80% of 5-minute momentary time samples across 3 consecutive weeks.
Baseline: 46%. Weekly means: 51%, 58%, 55%, 63%, 66%, 61%, 70%. Q1 mean 61%.
Progress: Adequate progress.

GOAL 3 - Reading comprehension
Given an 8th-grade level informational passage, Gunner will answer inferential questions with 70% accuracy on 4 of 5 probes.
Baseline: 40%. Probes: 45%, 50%, 40%, 60%, 55%.
Progress: Adequate progress; anticipated to meet goal by the annual review.

GOAL 4 - Adult interaction
Gunner will accept "no" or a delayed answer from an adult without arguing or leaving the area in 4 of 5 opportunities.
Baseline: 1 of 5. Current: 3 of 5 (staff tally, last two weeks).
Progress: Adequate progress.

BEHAVIOR SUMMARY

Verbal aggression decreased from 31 incidents in Q4 to 17 in Q1. Gunner moved from Level 2 to Level 3 on 09/28/2026. Return to his home high school requires 6 consecutive weeks at Level 4 and an ARC review.

RESTRAINT AND SECLUSION
One physical restraint on 09/03/2026 (11:42 a.m., 4 minutes, two CPI-trained staff) after Gunner threw a chair and attempted to strike a peer. Grandmother notified by phone the same day; written report sent within 24 hours per 704 KAR 7:160; debriefing meeting held 09/08/2026. Seclusion: none.

Accommodations in use: preferential seating near the door, break card (3 per block), chunked assignments, check-in/check-out with the behavior interventionist, read-aloud for tests except reading comprehension.

RELATED SERVICES
